correctness.rationale: The spectral classification follows for the stated characteristic factor and positive parameter regime. With P=z²+az+ah and Q=B(z+a), |P(iω)|²−|Q(iω)|² is the claimed quadratic in ω² and has exactly one positive zero because its constant term is negative. Zero itself is not a root since D(0,τ)=a(b−h)>0. At the positive zero the unit phase −P/Q gives the stated cosine and a sine with the sign of a²−ah+ω². That sign is positive: when a<h, evaluation of the frequency polynomial at a(h−a) gives ah(a²−B²)<0, so this argument lies below the positive zero. Hence the stated arccos branch gives all delays. At iω let A=P′/P−Q′/Q. Then D_z=P(A+τ), and d/dω(|P|²−|Q|²)=−2|P|² Im A>0 there. In particular D_z≠0, and for the simple root branch Re(1/z′)=−Im A/ω>0, proving a strict left-to-right crossing at every repetition. At zero delay the coefficients a+B and a(b−h) are positive; the extra root c−g is always negative. Every root in Re z≥0 obeys |P(z)|≤|Q(z)|, giving a uniform large-radius bound, so no right-half-plane roots enter from infinity, even as τ starts from 0. The argument principle and simple crossings give a jump by two, with 2n in the open half-plane at the n-th crossing. An independent exact-coefficient calculation for the stated example gave ω=0.80372740355465…, τ₀=1.95460579315185…, spacing=7.81755764378682…. The mathematics is linear and conditional on the supplied characteristic factor; the attribution and example in the underlying paper could not be independently checked against its full text.

value.rationale: For the stated model regime, eventual loss at a first Hopf point and permanent instability are different questions. A correct all-delay formula with exact counts, including the endpoints, excludes reentry and identifies how many unstable modes are present rather than merely exhibiting another crossing. This is a concrete linear investigation of a natural equilibrium; no novelty or value is attributed to the standard crossing rule itself.
